topics.title: Flyers don't trust their Thanksgiving flight will actually leave on time
topics.dek: A nationwide ground stop in mid-November disrupted about 46,000 flights, days before the busiest travel week of the year.

keyStat.label: flights canceled or delayed by one ground stop

topics.whyNow: Thanksgiving travel runs Nov 24–30, and the ground stop is still fresh in people's minds.
topics.frustration: It isn't only the delay itself. Travelers can't tell how fragile their trip is until it breaks: one system failure cascades across the whole country, rebooking options vanish at peak times, and they end up refreshing flight status apps for hours with no real plan B.
voices: Travelers say they check their flight status over and over in the days before leaving, just in case.
People heading home for the holiday say a cancellation doesn't mean being late. It means missing the dinner.
Travel companies point out that holiday delays aren't much worse than usual, but people's patience is much lower.

causes: Aging air-traffic systems are being blamed, and one failure spreads nationwide.

Delays early in the day cascade into the evening.
